Infer a reproduction matrix from generation-resolved transmission data

Source: R/inference.R
infer_R.Rd

Converts generation-resolved directed transmission counts into the sufficient statistics used by infer_R_sufficient(). For generation t, Y[t, i, j] records infections in destination i caused by source j. Source exposure at generation t is the number infected in source j at generation t - 1; the initially infected generation is therefore included in exposure for the first observed transmission generation.

Usage

infer_R(
  data,
  initial_cases,
  prior_shape = NULL,
  prior_rate = NULL,
  structural_zero = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with columns generation, source, destination, and transmissions. Generations are positive integers beginning with the first observed offspring generation.

initial_cases

A named vector of finite nonnegative integer counts for generation zero. Its names define the canonical community order.

prior_shape

A required finite positive scalar or matrix of Gamma prior shape parameters.

prior_rate

A required finite positive scalar or matrix of Gamma prior rate parameters.

structural_zero

Optional logical matrix identifying edges fixed at zero by design. Positive observations on those edges are rejected. A zero observed count is otherwise treated as a sampling zero, not a structural zero.

Value

An object of class routbreak_inference. In addition to the fields returned by infer_R_sufficient(), it contains the reconstructed array Y with dimensions generation by destination by source, named initial_cases, and the generation-by-community matrix infections_by_generation used to calculate previous-generation exposures.

Details

Missing source-destination rows are interpreted as zero transmissions. Duplicate generation-source-destination rows are rejected rather than silently aggregated.

Examples

transmissions <- data.frame(
  generation = rep(1L, 4),
  source = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
  destination = c("A", "A", "B", "B"),
  transmissions = c(12L, 4L, 3L, 16L)
)
fit <- infer_R(
  transmissions, initial_cases = c(A = 10, B = 20),
  prior_shape = 1, prior_rate = 1
)
fit$S
#>    A  B
#> A 12  4
#> B  3 16
fit$E
#>  A  B 
#> 10 20 
fit$mle
#>     A   B
#> A 1.2 0.2
#> B 0.3 0.8
